title: Spain Digital Nomad Visa 2026: Income & Routes
metaDescription: Spain digital nomad visa 2026: about 2,849 euros a month income, 200% of the minimum wage, plus 1,068 euros for a first dependent. Routes explained.
headline: Spain Digital Nomad Visa 2026: Income, Routes & Application

sections.title: What the visa is and who qualifies
sections.content:
Spain's digital nomad visa, launched in 2023 under the Startup Law, lets non-EU remote workers live in Spain while working for companies or clients outside Spain. At least 80% of a freelancer's income must come from non-Spanish clients, though up to 20% may come from Spain, and employees need a foreign employer that has operated for at least one year.

You also need a degree, vocational qualification or at least three years of professional experience, plus a remote working relationship of at least three months before applying. Applicants must have no Spanish tax residence in the previous five years and no criminal record, with certificates covering recent years of residence.

sections.title: Income thresholds for 2026
sections.content:
The main applicant needs about 2,849 euros a month in 2026, set at 200% of Spain's minimum interprofessional salary, with the exact figure moving whenever the minimum wage is updated, so confirm the current SMI before filing. Some guides cite a lower figure after the 2026 minimum-wage revision, which is why the consulate's current figure governs.

Dependents add 75% of the minimum wage, about 1,068 euros a month, for the first family member and 25%, about 356 euros, for each additional member. A family of four therefore needs roughly 4,632 euros a month, evidenced with payslips or invoices plus bank statements for the last three months.

sections.title: Two routes: consulate visa versus in-Spain permit
sections.content:
Applying at a Spanish consulate abroad gives a visa valid up to one year, which can later be converted into a residence permit. Applying while legally in Spain through the UGE, the large-companies unit, gives a three-year residence permit directly, renewable for two more years, and silence after the 20-day decision period counts as approval.

The consular fee is around 80 euros for most nationalities, though UK applicants pay a higher reciprocity fee, and the UGE fee is 73.26 euros. After arrival you register for a NIE foreigner identity number and a TIE residence card, and freelancers normally register as autonomo for social security.

sections.title: Taxes, stay and practical tips
sections.content:
Residents may qualify for Spain's special Beckham Law tax regime, a flat-rate scheme for qualifying inbound workers, but eligibility depends on your history and employment structure, so take advice before assuming it. The visa does not by itself grant permanent residence, which requires five years of legal residence, with citizenship timelines varying by nationality.

Prepare for sworn translations of foreign documents into Spanish, apostilles on criminal records, and health insurance with coverage matching the Spanish public system. File early: consulate appointment waits of two to eight weeks are common, and a complete file is the main thing that keeps the one-to-three-month process on track.

faqs.q: What is the minimum income for Spain's digital nomad visa in 2026?
faqs.a: The main applicant needs about 2,849 euros a month, set at 200% of Spain's minimum interprofessional salary, with the figure moving whenever the minimum wage is updated. Add about 1,068 euros a month for a first dependent and 356 euros for each additional dependent, so a family of four needs roughly 4,632 euros a month.

faqs.q: Can I apply for Spain's digital nomad visa from inside Spain?
faqs.a: Yes, if you are legally in Spain, including on a tourist Schengen stay, you can apply through the UGE for a three-year residence permit directly, renewable for two more years. The consular route instead gives a one-year visa that you later convert, and its first year does not count toward long-term residence if you wait to convert.

faqs.q: What experience or qualifications do I need?
faqs.a: You need a university degree, postgraduate qualification or vocational qualification, or proof of at least three years of professional experience in your field. Your remote working relationship must also be at least three months old at application, and your employer or main clients must have been operating for at least one year.

faqs.q: Can freelancers earn income from Spanish clients?
faqs.a: Yes, but only up to 20% of total income may come from clients in Spain; at least 80% must come from abroad. Freelancers evidence this with contracts or service agreements, invoices from the last three months, and bank statements showing the payments, plus proof that their main clients have operated for at least a year.

faqs.q: What is the Beckham Law and does it apply to nomad visa holders?
faqs.a: The Beckham Law is Spain's special tax regime for qualifying inbound workers, offering a flat tax rate instead of progressive rates for a fixed period. Eligibility depends on your employment structure and residence history, including no Spanish tax residence in the previous five years, so confirm your position with a tax adviser before relying on it.
